segments.flavor: the signature, low heat and high standards
segments.text:
Cyrus: Groove Kitchen. Low heat, high standards. Nothing leaves this kitchen cold.
Cyrus: The stool is open. The horns are coming.

segments.flavor: Cyrus narrates one step of tonight's dish as if it were the record's arrangement; Della rates the result
segments.text:
Cyrus: Onions in now, slow, the way the horns ease in on a good record.
Cyrus: Della would rate that a seven. She is not here. Nine. Play the horns.

segments.flavor: Della hums back a line from the last record and rates the bassline out of ten; Cyrus argues for the half point
segments.text:
Della: Hear that walk? Mmm. It goes down four steps and only climbs back three.
Cyrus: That missing step is the whole point. That is a seven at least.
Della: Six and a half. The bass player was thinking about his lunch.
Cyrus: So am I. Let it play.

segments.flavor: the Inheritance Skillet, seasoned by somebody's grandmother
segments.text:
Cyrus: The Inheritance Skillet arrives already seasoned. Somebody's grandmother did forty years of the work.
Della: [chuckle] Whose grandmother, exactly? That is a real question.
Cyrus: A grandmother. The skillet holds heat the way a good song holds a room.
Della: It weighs as much as a small oven. Lift with the knees.
Cyrus: Never soap it. Never lend it. Never ask about the grandmother.
Della: The Inheritance Skillet cannot be returned. It knows where you live now.
Cyrus: Heat it slow while this one plays.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a kitchen or dance product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Della
segments.text:
Cyrus: Sunday Gravy comes in a jar now. Somebody's grandmother, bottled, with her blessing.
Della: Her blessing cost them a fortune. She held out for six months.
Cyrus: Respect. It pours slow, it clings to the spoon, it hums a little.
Della: Gravy does not hum, Cyrus. A jar is not a substitute for a Sunday.
Cyrus: Warm it low. Horns are up next.

segments.flavor: the Leftover Report
segments.text:
Cyrus: Time for the Leftover Report. My neighbor came by twice since the last record.
Della: Twice. He has a schedule now. That is a man with a system.
Cyrus: First visit he took greens. Second visit he brought the empty bowl back.
Della: Empty? He returned it empty?
Cyrus: Washed, though. I will give him that. The man returns a clean bowl.
Della: A clean bowl is not payment, Cyrus. A clean bowl is the least.
Cyrus: He also fixed the door that sticks. So the ledger is fair.
Della: The ledger is generous. Put a record on before he knocks again.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as a dish on tonight's menu; Cyrus lists the ingredients
segments.text:
Cyrus: Let me read that last set back the way I would read a menu.
Della: Go on. You have been waiting all night to do this.
Cyrus: First course, light and sharp. A horn line you could cut with a fork.
Della: Second course was the heavy one. That bass sat down on the plate.
Cyrus: It did. Then dessert, which nobody asked for and everybody finished.
Della: That is a menu. Now stop describing food and feed the room.
Cyrus: Kitchen is open. Next plate.

segments.flavor: Lyle calls to correct one detail from the last break, then hangs up before anyone can answer
segments.text:
Cyrus: Before that fades, I want to say something about where it was recorded.
Della: Careful. Every time you say where, the phone rings.
Cyrus: It was cut in a room above a hardware store. Small room, big ceiling.
Lyle: Below. The room was below the hardware store. And the city is wrong.
Della: [sigh] Lyle. We have a doorbell. You could use the doorbell.
Lyle: Catalogue number ends in nine, not seven. Different pressing, different hiss, different...
Cyrus: And he is gone. Mid-word. The man leaves like a fade-out.
Della: He is never wrong, though. That is the infuriating part.
Cyrus: Never. Below the hardware store, then. Nine, not seven.
Della: The ceiling was big either way. Let it spin.

segments.flavor: the Sunday Six slow cooker, one setting: eventually
segments.text:
Cyrus: The Sunday Six slow cooker has one dial and one setting. Eventually.
Della: That is not a setting. That is a mood.
Cyrus: It is a philosophy. Put the food in at noon. Trust the afternoon.
Della: Trust is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
Cyrus: Six quarts. Heavy lid. Handles that do not burn your hands.
Della: The Sunday Six makes no promises about dinner time. Or dinner.
Cyrus: Lid on. Let the record do the waiting with us.

segments.flavor: Della hums back a line from the last record and rates the bassline out of ten; Cyrus argues for the half point
segments.text:
Cyrus: That bassline walked. I hummed it back myself and my hum was a crime.
Cyrus: Della is at the sink. In her absence I award it eight. Roll the next one.

segments.flavor: the Pot Watch
segments.text:
Cyrus: Pot Watch. Current status of the pot. Close. Very close.
Della: You said close two records ago. Close is not a temperature.
Cyrus: Close is a feeling. The lid is sweating. The kitchen smells honest.
Della: Honest kitchens still serve food eventually. Give me a number.
Cyrus: Twenty minutes.
Della: That is the same number as last hour. Your number never moves.
Cyrus: Good things do not move either. Let the record cover for me.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a kitchen or dance product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Della
segments.text:
Cyrus: A word about Clean Hands record sleeves. Paper that forgives a cook.
Della: Butter beads right off. Ask the man who ruined a whole soul boxset.
Cyrus: One box. One time. We agreed to stop discussing it on air.
Della: We agreed that you would stop. Music.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as a dish on tonight's menu; Cyrus lists the ingredients
segments.text:
Cyrus: That one simmered. Drums in first, then the organ, then a lot of patience.
Della: It was four minutes long, and you know that.
Cyrus: Felt like a stew. Onion bass, pepper in the guitar, horns laid on top.
Della: The horns were the garnish. Garnish does not carry a whole dish.
Cyrus: They carried it tonight. Next dish, coming up.

segments.flavor: Bernard's Academy, six weeks to a respectable two-step
segments.text:
Della: Bernard's Academy is taking students again. Six weeks to a respectable two-step.
Cyrus: Respectable is the word they chose. Not good. Respectable.
Della: Respectable is achievable. Good takes a lifetime and better shoes.
Cyrus: Week one is counting. Week two is the turn. Week three is confidence.
Della: Weeks four through six are apologies to your partner.
Cyrus: Bernard himself only attends on Thursdays. Nobody knows where he is otherwise.
Della: Results vary. Bernard varies. Refunds do not exist.
Cyrus: Practice to this next one. Slowly.

segments.flavor: Lyle calls to correct one detail from the last break, then hangs up before anyone can answer
segments.text:
Cyrus: The phone is blinking. That is my neighbor or the man from the record store.
Della: Your neighbor does not call. He just arrives with an empty bowl.
Lyle: It is Lyle. You said cayenne. The recipe you read takes white pepper.
Cyrus: Lyle, that is a kitchen matter. You correct records.
Lyle: I correct what is wrong. White pepper. And the B-side was better.
Della: [laugh] He hung up. He always hangs up before the good part.
Cyrus: White pepper it is. Let the B-side answer him.

segments.flavor: the Spice Cabinet
segments.text:
Cyrus: Open the Spice Cabinet. Tonight we match one spice to one instrument.
Della: Cumin.
Cyrus: Baritone sax. Low, warm, and it stays in the room after.
Della: That is right. Paprika.
Cyrus: Rhythm guitar. Not loud. But take it out and nothing works.
Della: Cinnamon.
Cyrus: Backing vocals. A little is a gift. A lot is a problem.
Della: You have thought about this more than a man should.
Cyrus: I have. Clove is a tambourine, and I will not be argued with.
Della: Nobody is arguing. Season the next one.

segments.flavor: Cyrus narrates one step of tonight's dish as if it were the record's arrangement; Della rates the result
segments.text:
Cyrus: I am building this in layers, and layers are just an arrangement you can eat.
Della: Here we go. Give me the first verse.
Cyrus: The bottom layer is rhythm. Potatoes, sliced thin, laid flat, no opinions.
Della: Potatoes have no opinions. Correct. Next.
Cyrus: Then the bass. Onion, butter, and time. That layer does the walking.
Della: Mm. I can hear that layer already. Keep going.
Cyrus: The top layer is the horns. Cheese, pepper, and a little showing off.
Della: Every horn section shows off. That is what horns are for.
Cyrus: Forty minutes covered, ten minutes open. Then we eat.
Della: Seven and a half for the bass layer. Now play something while we wait.

segments.flavor: the signature, soft butter and softer bass
segments.text:
Cyrus: You are in the Groove Kitchen, where the butter is soft and the bass is softer.
Cyrus: Mind the pot. Here is the band.

segments.flavor: Midnight Rub, sixteen things in one jar
segments.text:
Cyrus: Midnight Rub comes in a plain black jar. Sixteen things inside, and eleven of them stay secret.
Cyrus: One spoon per shoulder. No refunds, no ingredient list, and no questions asked. Rub it in, let this ride.

segments.flavor: Knife Skills
segments.text:
Cyrus: Knife Skills. Hold the onion like a record. Fingers curled, thumb behind, no hurry.
Della: The thumb part is the part people skip. Then they come back with a story.
Cyrus: Cut on the beat and every piece comes out the same size.
Della: Cut ahead of the beat and dinner is uneven, and so are you.
Cyrus: Slow hands, sharp blade. The board keeps time like a brush on a snare.
Della: That I would rate. Give me a beat to practice on.

segments.flavor: the signature, the whole menu and the whole promise
segments.text:
Cyrus: [gentle] Slow-cooked funk, served warm. That is the whole menu and the whole promise.
Cyrus: Groove Kitchen. The next plate is already warm.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a kitchen or dance product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Della
segments.text:
Cyrus: The Groove Kitchen wooden spoon. One piece of maple, and it outlives the cook.
Cyrus: Not a microphone. Two people have tried. Stir slow and let this next one move.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as a dish on tonight's menu; Cyrus lists the ingredients
segments.text:
Cyrus: On tonight's menu, that last one was the sweet course. Two horns, one organ, and no salt at all.
Cyrus: There was butter in that guitar, though. You could hear it melt. Send the next course out now.

segments.flavor: the Deep Pocket apron, one pocket fits a single
segments.text:
Cyrus: The Deep Pocket apron. Heavy canvas, four pockets, and one of them fits a single.
Della: A record. In your apron. Beside the spoons.
Cyrus: Where else would a man keep it? Close to the work.
Della: Grease, Cyrus. Grease is where you would keep it.
Cyrus: Double stitched. Straps cross the back so your neck stays free.
Della: Deep Pocket is not liable for whatever melts in the pocket.
Cyrus: Tie it on. Here comes the next one.

segments.flavor: Lyle calls to correct one detail from the last break, then hangs up before anyone can answer
segments.text:
Cyrus: Everybody calls that one the single. It sold the whole album.
Della: Phone. That is the phone. You said single out loud.
Lyle: B-side. It was the B-side. The single is the slow one nobody plays.
Cyrus: The B-side outsold it, though. That counts for something.
Lyle: It counts as a B-side. Goodbye.
Della: [sigh] He is correct and he is rude, both permanent. Back to the record.

segments.flavor: the Fridge Note
segments.text:
Cyrus: There is a note on the fridge again. Somebody writes to me at night.
Della: You write them. You write the notes and then you forget.
Cyrus: This one says do not touch the brown pot. Underlined twice.
Della: That is your handwriting. Tall letters, angry line.
Cyrus: Then past me is looking out for present me, and I respect that.
Della: Past you also wrote buy lemons, and there are no lemons.
Cyrus: Past me is a dreamer. The brown pot stays untouched either way.
Della: Read the next note after the record.

segments.flavor: Cyrus narrates one step of tonight's dish as if it were the record's arrangement; Della rates the result
segments.text:
Cyrus: The greens go in whole and they cook down to nothing. That is the long fade.
Della: A fade is a decision. Greens are just surrender.
Cyrus: Greens are patience. Forty minutes and the pot drops by half.
Della: So does a good outro. Everything gets quieter and nobody minds.
Cyrus: Pepper vinegar at the end. That is the last chord ringing out.
Della: Now that I will rate. Pepper vinegar is an eight.
Cyrus: An eight from you is a parade.
Della: Do not make it strange. Play the next one.

segments.flavor: Della hums back a line from the last record and rates the bassline out of ten; Cyrus argues for the half point
segments.text:
Cyrus: I want to enter something into the record. A formal appeal.
Della: The scale is not a court, Cyrus.
Cyrus: That bassline was perfect. Perfect means ten. You gave it eight and a half.
Della: Eight and a half is the highest I have given in years.
Cyrus: Then what is a ten? Describe it. I would like it in words.
Della: A ten would make me stop singing. Permanently. I would retire.
Cyrus: So the scale protects your job.
Della: [serious] The scale protects the music. If everything is a ten, nothing is.
Cyrus: Eight and a half stands, then. Under protest.
Della: Noted. Filed. Ignored.
Cyrus: Play it again and let the room decide.

segments.flavor: Aunt Verna's skillet cornbread mix
segments.text:
Della: Aunt Verna's skillet cornbread mix. One bag, one egg, one hot pan.
Cyrus: Verna does not use sugar. Verna has opinions about sugar.
Della: Verna has opinions about everything and she is right about most of it.
Cyrus: The crust comes up gold and loud. You can hear it break.
Della: Verna is not affiliated with any other Verna. Do not write to her.
Cyrus: Butter it warm. Music while it cools.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} as a dish on tonight's menu; Cyrus lists the ingredients
segments.text:
Cyrus: That last one, plated: smoked bass, sweet guitar on top, one pinch of salt.
Cyrus: Three ingredients. No garnish. That is the whole dish. Next course is coming.

segments.flavor: the Kitchen Timer nobody set
segments.text:
Della: Something is beeping. Cyrus, something in this kitchen is beeping.
Cyrus: That is the timer. I did not set it.
Della: Then who set it?
Cyrus: Nobody. It has been going off on its own for a while now.
Della: And you just let it?
Cyrus: I taste everything when it rings. Twice it was right.
Della: Twice. Out of how many?
Cyrus: Do not ruin it. The timer has earned its place. Roll the music.

segments.flavor: Lyle calls to correct one detail from the last break, then hangs up before anyone can answer
segments.text:
Cyrus: That horn section was the house band. They played that room nightly.
Lyle: Hired. One afternoon only. The house band was at a wedding.
Della: Lyle. We have not even said hello yet.
Lyle: Hello. Check the back of the sleeve. Bye.
Cyrus: Every time. The sleeve wins. Let the horns speak for themselves.

segments.flavor: Cyrus narrates one step of tonight's dish as if it were the record's arrangement; Della rates the result
segments.text:
Cyrus: Flour and fat in the pan, low, and we stir until it browns.
Della: How brown?
Cyrus: The color of a good snare. You smell it before you see it.
Della: A color is not a sound, Cyrus.
Cyrus: In this kitchen it is. The roux is the rhythm section.
Della: Then it is a six. It rushed the beat. Now let the band cook.

segments.flavor: the Countertop Six radio, one knob, one speaker
segments.text:
Cyrus: The Countertop Six kitchen radio. One knob, one speaker, and a dial that always stops here.
Cyrus: Metal case, cloth grille, and it survives a dropped pan every single time. Turn it up and stand back.

segments.flavor: Della hums back a line from the last record and rates the bassline out of ten; Cyrus argues for the half point
segments.text:
Della: Mmm. Hear that? The same note four times and it still went somewhere.
Cyrus: One string. He played that whole line on one string.
Della: Seven.
Cyrus: Seven? For one string? That is a man doing more with less.
Della: That is a man who did not want to move his hand.
Cyrus: Half a point for the economy. Half a point for the nerve.
Della: Half a point in total. Seven and a half, and that is final.
Cyrus: I will take it. Roll the tape.

segments.flavor: the House Rules
segments.text:
Cyrus: House rule of the night. Wash your hands, taste as you go, never rush a bassline.
Della: Three rules, and two of them are about the food. That is the ratio here.
Cyrus: The third one covers everything else. Rushing is the only sin in this kitchen.
Della: You rushed a pot once. I remember that pot.
Cyrus: One pot. Years ago. I have made my peace with it.
Della: The pot has not forgiven you. Play something slow and prove the rule.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a kitchen or dance product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Della
segments.text:
Cyrus: Word from the people at Sprung. They make a floor you install yourself.
Della: A floor. We are selling floors now.
Cyrus: Not the whole floor. Tiles. They go over the floor you already have.
Della: Why would a person need a second floor on top of the first?
Cyrus: Because the first one does not give. A good floor answers your feet.
Della: Mine answers. It says stop.
Cyrus: Sprung tiles lock together in an afternoon. No glue, no nails, no landlord.
Della: No landlord means nobody told the landlord.
Cyrus: Nobody needs to. They come up in spring and go down in the fall.
Della: Sprung is not responsible for the neighbor below you. Nobody is.
Cyrus: Lay them down and put this next one on.

segments.flavor: the signature, Della's scale
segments.text:
Della: Groove Kitchen. Every bassline gets a number from me. None of them get ten.
Cyrus: She means it. I have never once seen a ten.
Della: Sit down. Let the record talk.

segments.flavor: Sole Food shoes, built for kitchen floors
segments.text:
Cyrus: Sole Food shoes were built for kitchen floors and tested on a Saturday.
Della: Tested by who? I want a name.
Cyrus: Forty people, one church hall, and a floor that has seen things.
Della: That is a test. I accept that test.
Cyrus: Leather sole, soft heel, and they slide exactly as far as you ask.
Della: Sole Food cannot make you graceful. Nothing can. Ask Bernard.
Cyrus: Lace them up. The floor is open.

segments.flavor: the Second Helping
segments.text:
Cyrus: Second Helping. Once a night we go back for something we already had.
Della: It is the only greedy thing this station does.
Cyrus: It is not greed. It is confirmation. Some records improve on the second plate.
Della: Most do not. Most are a one-plate record, and that is fine.
Cyrus: A one-plate record is still a record.
Della: So what gets the second helping?
Cyrus: The one with the horn line that would not leave me alone.
Della: Good pick. Go on then. Twice in one night.
